chunks: And ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī ʿAbdillāh asked al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام:
about the wind, the darkness that occurs in the sky, and eclipses
So al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام said: “Their salat (prayer) is the same.”

key_terms.الرِّيحِ: wind or storm mentioned as a cause for a prescribed salat
key_terms.السَّمَاءِ: the sky, where these signs appear
key_terms.الظُّلْمَةِ: darkness appearing in the sky as an extraordinary sign
key_terms.سَوَاءٌ: the same or equal in ruling
key_terms.صَلَاتُهُمَا: their salat, meaning the prayer related to these occurrences

ai.seo_question: Is the salat for wind, darkness in the sky, and eclipses the same in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the salat prescribed for phenomena such as strong wind, darkness in the sky, and eclipse is the same. It presents a concise legal ruling in matters of devotional practice related to extraordinary natural signs.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1509 - Abdul-Rahman ibn Abi Abdullah asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as)
about windstorms, darkness in the sky, and eclipses.
Imam (as) replied: "The prayer for all of them is the same”.
